assertions.description: window.maximize is a function on the Window instance, with the Promise-returning receiver defined by the current Window Management Working Draft.
window.minimize is a function on the Window instance, with the Promise-returning receiver defined by the current Working Draft.
window.restore is a function on the Window instance, with the Promise-returning receiver defined by the current Working Draft.
window.setResizable is a function on the Window instance. The current Working Draft defines setResizable(boolean) as Promise-returning; invocation checks are separate from exposure.
Exactly one display-state value—normal, minimized, maximized, or fullscreen—matches the current browsing context when the media feature applies.
Exactly one resizable value—true or false—matches and reports whether the current top-level application window is user-resizable.
window.maximize(), minimize(), and restore() resolve with undefined when their requested OS window-state changes succeed, or reject with NotAllowedError on the Working Draft's denied paths.
assertions.test: Not run automatically: resolution requires an installed desktop PWA window, real window-management permission UI, transient user activation, the DesktopPWAsAdditionalWindowingControls runtime feature, and a cooperating window manager.

assertions.description: window.setResizable(false) resolves after a successful OS operation and the resizable media feature reports false; setResizable(true) restores a true report.
assertions.test: Not run automatically: method resolution and resulting media-state changes require an installed top-level app window, real permission UI, the runtime feature, and a cooperating window manager.

assertions.description: A display-state MediaQueryList fires a change event when a genuine transition changes whether that query matches.
assertions.test: Not run automatically: a genuine window-state transition requires an implementing installed app plus OS window-manager cooperation; UI toggles and simulated values are not evidence.
